newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says MPs killing attack on democracy.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says MPs killing attack on democracy.

text.p: Sri Lankan political parties on Monday condemned the killing of an opposition lawmaker near the eastern town of Trincomalee and said it was aimed at disrupting the political process to end the country's ethnic war.

United National Party (UNP) parliamentarian Mohammed Moharoof and five others, including a four-year-old boy, were killed when gunmen ambushed their jeep between Trincomalee and the nearby beach resort of Nilaveli on Sunday.
Police blamed separatists Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) for the killing and said 25 suspects had been taken in for questioning from villages in the area where Moharoof was shot.

"This appears to be a calculated act to get rid of political leaders in the eastern province who are attempting to help the government democratically in solving the ethnic problem peacefully and ending the conflict," Dharmasiri Senanayke, general secretary of Sri Lanka Freedom Party (SLFP) said in a statement.
The SLFP is the main constituent of the ruling People's Alliance coalition government.

The LTTE are fighting a 13-year-old war against the government for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE put the toll higher.

Political sources said Moharoof's murder, which followed the killing of a Tamil United National Front (TULF) lawmaker in Trincomalee earlier in the month, showed the separatists' resolve to block the government's proposed constitutional reforms.
The government has proposed a package of reforms aimed at devolving more powers to the minorities in an attempt to end the bloody ethnic crisis.
TULF parliamentarian Arunasalam Thangathurai was killed in a grenade attack in Trincomalee on July 5. Police blamed the LTTE for that attack too.

The new constitution is being debated in a parliamentary select committee, but the process has slowed down due to disagreements between Tamil and Moslem parties, and between the ruling People's Alliance and the UNP.
The committee is negotiating key issues such as devolution of power to minorities and demarcation of proposed new councils in Sri Lanka's north and east.

Political sources said Tamil and Moslem parties were close to reaching an agreement on the devolution and on a separate Moslem area to be demarcated within the Tamil enclave in the east. "It (Moharoof's killing) is a fascist act aimed at dividing the Tamil and Moslem communities," Douglas Devananda, leader of the Eelam People's Democratic Party was quoted as saying by the state radio.

The LTTE, who are fighting Sri Lankan troops in the northern Wanni region, have of late increased their activities in the port town of Trincomalee, site of a 1995 rebel attack on navy boats that led to the breakdown of peace talks between them and the government.
